subagent_tasks.description: bounded Plans/**/*.md scan for doc discovery / owner-unknown groups

docs_or_topics_assigned: Because this document is cross-cutting, its stale hostability rules can easily reintroduce drift into:
Example pattern: `route_target` / `OpenSubject` exist, but precedence, reject rules, examples, and scoped-resolution rules are still missing.
OpenCode limitations are now source-verified enough that they should be treated as hard architectural constraints unless the bridge changes:
Preview restore identity is subject-first, while the broader route/open owner docs still do not define the named route/open primitives that would explain it consistently.
Reconcile HITL restore/state docs so restart behavior restores blocked approval episodes rather than a competing tier-boundary request object.
Reconcile `cmd.graph.approve_hitl` and `cmd.graph.deny_hitl` away from `request_id` args and toward runtime-native blocked identity.
Reconcile widget layout persistence keys so stale non-Progress Orchestrator widget-layout keys are not left as live canon.
Run Graph and Orchestrator are still said to aggregate by `tier_id` and `attempt_id?`
That means the main owner gap is no longer field names first. It is scope and owner identity.
The current unresolved blocker inventory therefore remains at eight blocker families, nineteen affected docs, and fifty underlying evidence refs.
The graph approval commands do not currently have one stable args contract even before considering the broader runtime-model rewrite.
The handoff addenda already assume attempt-native execution identity, but the core narrative still teaches tier-centric scope resolution.
The owner doc says runtime identity is canonical, while still anchoring key override and selection concepts to `tier`.
The owner docs already settled the canonical requested/effective runtime identity field names:
The remaining work is now mostly about collapsing overlapping canon and fixing exact broken references, payloads, and command contracts.
The rerun makes it clear that the concern/action/governance tranche is missing not just "some schemas", but the following concrete families:
This is the cleanest remaining bridge between the old HITL plan and the new blocked/runtime command model.
This pass kept the blocker-family count at eight and did not add new blocker families, but it removed one overstated unresolved item and made several owner/consumer defects more exact.
This seam is now purely consumer-side. The runtime command layer already has the stronger model.
`00-plans-index.md` still under-routes rewrite-critical owner docs, especially around Multi-Account, Provider, and Orchestrator packet ownership.
`Executor_Protocol.md` is already ahead of `human-in-the-loop.md` on this seam.
`OpenCode_Deep_Extraction.md` sharpens the server-global SSE / fixed working-directory / session-scoped compaction and approvals / ephemeral session identity issues into direct PM obligations.
`Runtime Recovery Canonicalization Gate Addendum` appears twice with the same body
`canon_inventory.json` now lags the refined blocker wording again, so the next useful stage is `Ledger Condenser`.
`execution_role` absent in many key owner/consumer docs
`persona_override_owner_id` needs owner-level cleanup so it no longer teaches `tier_id` as a canonical scope anchor.
`projection_freshness` and `projection_health` already exist; the missing transfer is the operational UI/gating/fallback layer, not simply "invent trust states."
`usage.jsonl` and canonical usage discussion still center `tier_id`

demote `tier` wording to compatibility or derived decomposition context
extend the effective-resolution and handoff records to the newer identity layers already established in research
newer canonical runtime records and projections
no named `route_target` / `OpenSubject` contract tie even though subject-first preview identity already exists
project-summary, escalation, blocked-owner, and resurfacing rules
provider-account policy and requested/effective identity fields are closer to the rewrite direction than several consumer docs
redb persistence text keyed to `request_id`, `tier_id`, `tier_type`, `request_kind`, and `allowed_actions`
